w: This hillside cemetery above Deadwood holds the graves of Wild Bill Hickok, Calamity Jane and lawman Seth Bullock, alongside other notable figures of the Wild West. By long tradition the American flag flies over the grounds around the clock, rather than only from sunrise to sunset.
s: Wild Bill Hickok and Calamity Jane's hillside graves
_facts: Burial place of Wild Bill Hickok, Calamity Jane, and Seth Bullock
Flag flown 24 hours a day by long tradition

w: Proprietor Tom Miller opened this upscale saloon and theater in Deadwood on September 10, 1876; it soon hosted town meetings alongside its stage shows. Miller kept buying neighboring properties until he went bankrupt in 1878, when the Bella Union split into a grocery store and an upstairs hall, Mechanics' Hall.
s: 1876 gold-rush saloon that doubled as the town hall
_facts: Opened September 10, 1876 by proprietor Tom Miller
Upscale saloon and theater also used for town meetings
Became a grocery store and Mechanics' Hall meeting room

w: This 31-foot stone tower on the edge of the Black Hills National Forest outside Deadwood was dedicated July 4, 1919, as the first memorial built anywhere to honor Theodore Roosevelt. Locally known as the Friendship Tower, it stands on a six-foot platform overlooking the hills Roosevelt was closely tied to.
_facts: 31-foot stone tower (with a six-foot platform) in Black Hills National Forest
First tribute built to Theodore Roosevelt's memory
Also called the Roosevelt Friendship Monument

w: Founded in 1930 by former Deadwood mayor W.E. Adams as a gift to the city, this is the Black Hills' oldest history museum. Its cases hold Potato Creek Johnny's Gold Nugget, the Thoen Stone and the J.B. Haggin Locomotive, alongside relics of Wild Bill, Calamity Jane and the gold rush.
s: Black Hills' oldest museum, gold-rush relics and all
_facts: Founded 1930 by former mayor W.E. Adams, still city property
Holds Potato Creek Johnny's Gold Nugget, the Thoen Stone, J.B. Haggin Locomotive
Ranked #3 in True West Magazine's 2009 Top 10 Western Museums

w: Built around 1895 by Seth Bullock, Deadwood's first sheriff, and business partner Sol Star at a cost of 40,000 dollars, this corner hotel at Wall and Main Street is the oldest in town. Twenty-eight of its original 63 rooms survive, now alongside a casino and restaurant.
s: Sheriff Seth Bullock's 1895 hotel, still Deadwood's oldest
_facts: Built c.1895 by Seth Bullock (Deadwood's first sheriff) and Sol Star
Cost about $40,000; oldest hotel in Deadwood
Corner of Wall Street and Main Street
